readout_other: Hind-paw withdrawal reflex to iFU; comparison thermal (Hargreaves) withdrawal latency test
direction_notes: Neuropathic (pSNL) rats preferentially withdrew their injured paw from iFU at lower iFU intensity thresholds than sham-surgery or normal-control rats, with greater sensitivity and specificity for the ipsilateral paw.

exposures.label: iFU paw-withdrawal threshold testing in partial sciatic nerve ligation (pSNL), sham-surgery and normal-control rats

target.label: the plantar surface of the paw

timing.protocol_description: In the absence of a hind paw withdrawal response, the intensity of ultrasound was increased in increments beginning at approximately 30% of the previous intensity, tapering to 10%, starting with an initial acoustic intensity of approximately 10 W/cm2. After identification of the iFU threshold value, both hind paws were tested in a serial fashion for their withdrawal responses to that amount of iFU for an additional six iFU applications, with at least 30 s between each application.

source_quotes.n_subjects: We partially ligated the sciatic nerve within the right hind paws of 33 Sprague–Dawley rats (180–200 mg, Taconic) following the surgical protocol of Seltzer et al.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: On days 5 and 7 after surgery, we habituated sets of three rats to their free-ranging presence within a cage containing three separate enclosures, each with a wiremesh bottom.
source_quotes.safety_notes: We have as well, to a larger cohort, again without incident (Dickey et al. 2012).
source_quotes.exposures[0].target.label: This time, we applied individual acoustic pulses of length 0.2 s to the plantar surface of the paw, using ultrasound gel (Aquasonic 100 ultrasound transmission gel; Parker Laboratories Inc., Fairfield, NJ, USA) to ensure adequate coupling.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: We created the iFU signal (individual ultrasound pulses with a center frequency of 1.15 MHz, each lasting for 0.2 s) with two function generators (HP33120A; Hewlett-Packard, Palo Alto, CA, USA), amplified by a power amplifier (ENI A150; ENI, Rochester, NY, USA) whose signal we transmitted directly to the transducer.

flags.reason: Paper gives group sizes (33 pSNL, 30 sham, 12 normal control) but never states a combined total exposed to ultrasound, so group sizes are listed rather than summed.

Value reported is the mean iFU threshold intensity found per group (Table 3), not a fixed applied stimulus level; the device's intensity was titrated up from about 10 W/cm2 in each session until a withdrawal threshold was reached.

Paper reports intensity as I_SATA (spatially averaged, temporally averaged), which does not exactly match either the isppa or ispta schema fields; recorded here under ispta_w_cm2 as the closest match.

Surgery for the pSNL and sham groups was performed under deep isoflurane anesthesia, but the iFU behavioural testing itself (5-7+ days later) was performed on awake, unanesthetized animals; anaesthesia field reflects the testing condition.
